Tool Setup and Instances

Understand Tool Instances

A Tool Instance is a named set of instrument settings in a Template. A Template can contain multiple instances of the same Tool Type, such as two Meters instances for voltage and current.

Information Storage
Instance and instrument setup Template
Executable path Local computer, shared by Tool Type
Live Resource Local computer, per instance

Setup sections

Tool Instance
  +-- Tool-specific setup
  +-- Background Streaming (initially collapsed)
  +-- Live Device (initially expanded)

Each instance has its own bordered card and starts expanded. Use + / − to collapse or expand it. Tool Instance Summary, above Add Tool Instance, counts instances by Tool Type, including types not configured locally. Unused types are omitted, and the summary is hidden when there are no instances.

Within each instance, tool settings come first, followed by Background Streaming, then Live Device, with separators around Background Streaming. Both sections have independent − / + controls. Background Streaming starts collapsed; Live Device starts expanded. Expand Background Streaming and select Enable Background Streaming to show the supported Background options. Unsupported Tool Types keep this checkbox disabled and show an explanation. Use Worker and Capture actions to control background streaming and data recording.

Group and card expansion states persist while editing, switching tabs, or collapsing an outer instance. Successful New Template or Open Template restores the default states, including External Tools cards. These UI states are not saved in the Template or local settings.

Add and name an instance

Add Tool Instance has a Tool type (select from list) dropdown that offers only Tool Types configured in Tools, including those with a Missing or Error status. With no configured Tool Type, adding an instance is disabled. Existing instances remain visible when their Tool Type is not locally configured, with a warning that disappears after configuration.

Expand any Tool Instance to edit Display Name (optional). Leave it blank to use the default instance ID. Names may include Chinese, English, numbers, and spaces, and different instances may share a name. The Setup title and Workflow Target options update immediately; the original Instance ID remains visible, including when collapsed. Target options keep any available model and serial information. Sequence summaries that show a target also show its name and ID; action and parameter summaries keep their existing format. Names are saved with the Template and restored on loading. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed on leaving the field or saving; clearing the name or entering only whitespace restores the ID. Editing is disabled while busy. Renaming does not change Workflow references, Simulation/Live mode, or saved Live Resources. Wavegen names can be saved even though its runtime actions are not yet supported.

Numeric fields use direct typing and native ArrowUp / ArrowDown stepping; spinner buttons are hidden.

Meters measurement setup

Meters Measurement Setup starts expanded; use − / + to hide or show its measurement and trigger settings without hiding Background Streaming or Live Device. These settings apply to Foreground or Background as supported by the selected mode. The current Setup controls:

Field Choices and purpose
Measurement DC Voltage or DC Current
Range Mode Auto or Manual
Manual Range Fixed choices supplied by the tool, not arbitrary text
NPLC 0.02, 0.2, 1, 10, 100; measurement integration time
Auto Zero On, Off, Once
DCV Input Impedance Voltage: Not specified, Default, 10 MΩ, Auto
Current Terminal Current: Not specified, 3 A terminal, 10 A terminal
VM Comp Slope Voltage/current: Not specified, Positive, Negative; unspecified keeps the current setting

Measurement and trigger modes

Choose whether to enable Background Streaming first. Foreground uses Single, one reading per Measure.

Mode Settings
Single (foreground) One trigger per Measure
Software, Immediate, External (background Simple) Finite sources use Max Samples
Software Custom, Immediate Custom, External Custom (background) Sample Count, optional Buffer Drain Size, Allow Buffer Overflow Risk; finite sources use Trigger Count
External / External Custom Optional Hardware Trigger Slope and Hardware Trigger Delay (s); unspecified uses tool defaults

Unsupported modes are disabled when model capabilities are available. Known reading-memory limits are shown. Planned readings above capacity display Reading memory exceeded and require explicit risk acceptance.

Measurement fields stay visible; inapplicable fields are disabled. The external meters-tool remains authoritative for the actual model capability and numeric limits. Desktop does not replace its capability database. In Simulation, capability choices come from the meter simulator profile rather than a saved Live meter identity. Live uses the saved identity when available.

Warning: Custom acquisition can lose data

In a Custom mode, selecting Allow Buffer Overflow Risk explicitly accepts possible unrecoverable data loss. High Buffer Overflow Risk Accepted appears whenever it is selected, even below the memory limit or before capabilities are available. Samples can be lost whenever acquisition outpaces the Worker's draining of reading memory; lower NPLC can increase that risk. Conversely, planned readings above capacity may still be captured completely if draining keeps up. Exceeding the planned capacity alone does not confirm overflow.

If a finite Custom acquisition loses samples, the Worker may keep waiting for missing samples after all planned triggers finish and may not finish naturally. This does not necessarily mean it has stopped responding: it may still accept existing Workflow or Worker Stop controls. Use those controls to end the operation as appropriate; Stop cannot recover lost data. These warnings apply in both Simulation and Live. The waiting behavior has been reproduced in Simulation; the same behavior has not been confirmed on physical instruments.

Neither summary.ok=true nor process exit code 0 guarantees that all expected readings were captured. Check Captured, Expected Readings, Stop Reason and Data Integrity together. Allow Risk does not ensure overflow monitoring is active, and Meters Setup has no separate monitoring control. Without monitoring results, absence of a detected overflow is not evidence of no data loss.

Configure Live Resources

A Live Resource is the real device address for an instance, stored locally. Last-known model and serial information is not a current connection check.

Tool Specify the connection
Meters, Powers, Scopes Select VISA Backend, then List Resources or enter manually
Serial UART COM Port or TCP Host / Port; see Serial steps
Wavegen Workflow execution is not supported
  1. Expand Live Device.
  2. Choose the applicable backend or transport.
  3. List or enter the address and check the device information.
  4. Select Save Resource; use Clear Resource to remove the saved connection.

VISA Backend and unsaved settings

Each supported instance has its own VISA Backend: System VISA (the default, including older configurations) or PyVISA-py (@py). Choose the backend before List Resources. Changing it immediately clears that instance's resource and identity drafts, discovery results and errors, and old Powers Device Status. Other instances are unaffected. The saved configuration stays unchanged until Save Resource, which saves the backend, resource and identity together. List resources again or enter a resource manually, then save; addresses from different backends are not converted or matched. Unsaved changes block Live runs and invalidate the previous Live Preflight result.

The backend is local to this machine and is not included in Templates. Simulation does not use it. If the selected backend is unavailable, discovery or connection fails with an error; Desktop does not switch backends automatically.

Live Resources always represent machine-local real hardware. Simulation does not require or use them, but you may list, edit, and save one for a future Live run without switching Execution Mode. Desktop does not create a fake simulator resource in local configuration.

Model identity and capabilities

Powers discovery may provide a canonical model ID. Desktop saves it with the last-known local resource identity and queries powers-tool capabilities --model offline to show available protection controls and channels. The Setup page does not connect to an instrument for this query. If the model ID or capabilities are unavailable in Live, select and save a supported Live Resource to enable new protection settings. In Simulation, Desktop queries powers-tool for the existing Powers simulator model, so Protection Setup does not require discovery or a saved resource. Existing Template settings remain visible when the current model does not support them.

Read & Drain Errors

Open Live Device in a Powers, Meters, or Scopes instance and select Read & Drain Errors in Error Queue. Meters requires a CLI with the read-errors command. Desktop checks the CLI and any known saved Meters model without connecting to the instrument. If you replace the Meters executable at the same path, select Refresh in Tools to check support again. In Live, save a discovered Scopes resource so Desktop can verify model support.

  • Simulation uses the Tool's simulator and displays NO HARDWARE I/O.
  • Live uses the saved Live Resource and VISA Backend, even if the Resource fields show a draft. The confirmation identifies the saved address. Reading removes the returned entries from the instrument's queue without issuing *CLS or clearing other instrument status.

All instances' buttons are disabled from Workflow start through stopping and cleanup. The diagnostic is manual and its results are shown only in Setup.

The result lists original error codes and messages in read order.

Result Meaning
Queue Empty First read confirms empty
Drained Entries were read and queue confirmed empty
Not Fully Drained 20-read limit reached without confirming empty
Failed Shows the failure and preserves returned entries

A connection failure during a read may mean the instrument removed an entry before returning it.

Powers protection setup

Protection Setup is optional. Within a Powers Tool Instance, use + beside Protection Setup to expand the group, which starts collapsed. Protection fields and the Device area, including Device Status, Refresh Status, Protection Summary, channel protection status and clear actions, and related messages and results, expand and collapse together. Live Device, VISA Backend, Live Resource and resource discovery controls and messages, and Remove Tool Instance and its workflow reference restriction remain visible. Collapsing preserves protection settings, runtime status and operation results without reading or operating the instrument. Select Use Protection Setup to edit supported fields. This single checkbox applies to the whole instance; new instances start unchecked with all fields disabled. Selecting it alone does not store any protection data or checkbox state in the Template. All channels reported by powers-tool are shown in aligned rows, together with any channels already configured in the Template. Each row shows OVP Voltage, OCP, OCP Delay, and OCP Delay Trigger. Unsupported controls remain visible but are disabled. Existing unsupported values are displayed with a warning and preserved when saving; the external tool still validates actual model support and limits.

Protection fields

Field Purpose
OVP Voltage (V) Overvoltage protection threshold; enter a supported voltage.
OCP Overcurrent protection: On or Off.
OCP Delay (s) Protection delay in seconds; subject to model limits.
OCP Delay Trigger Start the delay on Setting Change or CC Transition, as supported by the model.

Clear and save settings

An empty numeric field or Unchanged leaves that instrument setting unchanged and is not stored in the Template. Only configured channels and fields are saved. Existing Protection Setup opens with the checkbox checked. Clearing the last setting removes that channel's record; clearing all settings returns to an empty setup, unchecks Use Protection Setup, and disables the fields. Unchecking it also clears the entire Protection Setup and returns all fields to Unchanged. Channel rows stay visible according to capabilities; there are no Add Channel or Remove Channel controls. Protection Setup and Device Status tables show plain channel numbers under Channel; confirmations and clear plans use Channel 1. Workflow Sequence compact summaries retain CH1.

Protection setup execution order

In both modes, a referenced Powers instance with Protection Setup requests Safe-Off, reads Protection Status, applies settings one channel at a time only when status is clear, then starts Workflow steps. A reported trip blocks the run; Orchestrator never clears it automatically. The final Safe-Off still runs. In Simulation these operations use powers-tool's simulate/planning contract, so they validate sequencing without real hardware I/O. To fail a Workflow on a trip detected during execution, add a Power Protection Status step followed by Assert.

Live safety checks

Before a Live run, every referenced supported Tool Instance must have a non-empty saved resource. Two referenced instances may not use the same resource in one run. Live confirmation displays each referenced instance and Tool Type, saved backend and resource, and available last-known identity. If the backend or resource changes after confirmation, the run is rejected and must be confirmed again.

For a DC Current measurement using the 10 A terminal, Live confirmation also asks you to verify that the physical leads are connected to the 10 A terminal.

Powers device status and clearing protection

Expand Protection Setup to show the Device area and Device Status. Live Device / Live Resource controls remain below it in both Simulation and Live modes, including when Protection Setup is collapsed. The execution mode badge appears in the Tool Instance heading. Device Status is runtime-only and is not saved in the Template. Opening Setup does not connect to a Worker and there is no background polling. A single Protection Summary panel groups aggregate Protection, OVP, and OCP. These and per-channel values show — until status is read, then show CLEAR / OK or TRIPPED as reported. Channel rows include offline model capabilities, existing Template settings, and channels returned by a successful Refresh Status, which also updates their values. Simulation uses the simulator channels without a saved Live Resource. Live uses the saved model identity without connecting to hardware to build the rows; if capabilities are unavailable, configured channels remain visible and no other channels are guessed before Refresh. Even without a saved model identity, a successful Refresh displays the actual returned channels and makes reported trip channels eligible for Clear Protection under the usual rules. Switching Execution Mode clears stale values back to — and shows the channels known for the selected mode.

Simulation: generate a clear plan

In Simulation, Refresh Status starts the configured powers-tool simulate Worker and does not require a saved Live Resource. Generate Clear Plan... is available for every simulator-supported channel, even when status is not tripped. After confirmation, Orchestrator sends simulated Safe-Off All and clear-protection for the selected channel, then shuts down without rereading status. The result is shown as PLAN GENERATED · SIMULATION and NO HARDWARE I/O. Show Plan presents the target channel, Safe-Off first, protection clear, outputs remaining OFF, and no hardware I/O as a short operator preview. It does not display raw JSON or instrument commands. No real protection latch was changed.

Live: refresh and clear protection

In Live, Refresh Status uses a temporary Powers connection and the saved Live Resource and backend. Unsaved Live Resource or backend changes must be saved before Refresh Status or Clear Protection can be used. Device Status prompts you to save the Live Resource in the controls below when no resource is saved or draft changes are unsaved.

Each channel row has a fixed Action column. Generate Clear Plan... is enabled for simulator-supported channels when no operation is busy. In Live, Clear Protection... remains visible but disabled before Refresh Status and when the channel has no reported OVP or OCP trip. It becomes enabled for a reported trip when no Workflow or manual operation is busy, and always requires explicit confirmation. Orchestrator first performs Safe-Off All, clears only the selected channel protection latch, then rereads the full status. Clear Protection does not fix the cause of a trip and never turns an output back on. If the latch remains tripped, the status remains visible as unresolved; if the reread reports an output still ON, Desktop shows that state and a warning rather than hiding it or automatically changing it.

Refresh Status and Clear Protection are unavailable while a Workflow or another manual external operation is active. If remote clear is unsupported for the model, clear the protection latch from the instrument front panel and then use Refresh Status.

Scopes acquisition and channel setup

Scopes Setup is optional. New instances start with all settings Unchanged. Acquisition Setup and Channel Configuration start collapsed; use each heading's + / − independently. Collapsing preserves settings, and Live Resource remains outside both groups. Choose Acquisition Type (Normal, Average, High Resolution, or Peak); Average Count is editable only with Average. Channel rows provide Input Coupling, Probe Ratio, Bandwidth Limit, Waveform Invert, and Channel Units. Only explicit settings are saved, applied, and read back. Blank values and Unchanged send no commands.

Setup fields

Field Purpose and choices
Acquisition Type Acquisition mode: Normal, Average, High Resolution, Peak; subject to model support.
Average Count Number of acquisitions to average; editable only in Average and must be a supported integer.
Input Coupling Input coupling: AC or DC.
Probe Ratio Probe attenuation ratio; enter the value appropriate for the probe and supported by the model.
Bandwidth Limit Bandwidth limiting: On or Off.
Waveform Invert Waveform inversion: On or Off.
Channel Units Channel units: Volt or Amp.

Acquisition Setup contains the first two fields; Channel Configuration sets the remaining fields per channel. All fields default to Unchanged or blank; only explicitly selected values are saved and sent to the instrument. The tool supplies the actual supported limits.

Model support, readback and errors

The controls use offline Scopes capabilities. Simulation uses Scopes' default Keysight DSOX4024A profile. Live uses the canonical model ID saved with the selected Resource. Unknown or unavailable capability information disables new settings with an explanation. Unsupported fields remain visible and disabled; changing models preserves existing settings. Scopes validates actual model support and instrument limits when applying Setup. The run reports Setup FAIL if a readback fails, is missing, or differs from the requested value. The error identifies the instance and, for channel settings, the channel. Workflow steps start only after Setup succeeds. For example, if you set Channel 2 Waveform Invert to On and leave the other settings Unchanged, Setup verifies Channel 2 inversion before the Workflow starts.

Serial communication setup

Choose UART (COM Port) or TCP Client in Communication Setup. Communication settings belong to the Template; COM Port or TCP Host/Port is stored locally in Live Device.

Interface Field Purpose and choices
UART Baud Rate Positive integer transmission rate; new instance: 115200. Match the device.
UART Data Bits Bits per character: 5, 6, 7, 8; default 8.
UART Parity None (default), Odd or Even parity checking.
UART Stop Bits 1 (default) or 2 stop bits.
UART Flow Control None (default), Software or Hardware.
UART Timeout (ms) Non-negative integer I/O timeout in milliseconds; default 1000.
TCP Connect Timeout (ms) Positive integer connection timeout; displayed default 3000.
TCP I/O Timeout (ms) Positive integer communication I/O timeout; displayed default 1000.

Match UART settings to the device. TCP has no discovery; Simulation needs no Host or Port. See Serial steps for RX completion and timeout rules.
